From November 1969 to June 1971 a group of Native American activists called Indians of All Tribes occupied Alcatraz Island in San Francisco Bay, the site of a closed federal prison. They claimed it under an old treaty right to unused federal land.

The occupiers, many of them students, offered to buy the island for 24 dollars in glass beads and cloth, mocking the legend of the Dutch purchase of Manhattan for New Amsterdam. They called for a Native university and cultural centre and drew national attention.

The occupation ended when the government removed the last occupiers. But it inspired the Red Power movement and protests such as Wounded Knee in 1973. In 1970 President Nixon ended the federal policy of termination of tribes, opening an era of self-determination after the Dawes Act and the Ghost Dance era of loss.
